q: The debates on the future strategy of the national movement after the withdrawal of the Civil Disobedience Movement occurred in how many stages, and around what respective questions?
o: Two stages — the immediate post-CDM strategy (1934-35), and office acceptance after the 1937 provincial elections
Three stages, the last dealing with the Quit India Movement
Two stages, both dealing exclusively with communal representation
One stage focused solely on complete independence

q: Which nationalists advocated participation in elections to the Central Legislature (due in 1934) as a way to maintain political morale during the non-mass-struggle phase?
o: Bhagat Singh and Chandra Shekhar Azad
M.A. Ansari, Asaf Ali, Bhulabhai Desai, S. Satyamurthy and B.C. Roy
Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Bose
Muhammad Ali Jinnah and the Muslim League

q: Jawaharlal Nehru, representing the leftist trend within Congress, described the withdrawal of Civil Disobedience and any move towards council entry as:
o: A minor administrative matter of no ideological significance
The only viable path to eventual independence
"A spiritual defeat", "a surrender of ideals", and "a retreat from revolutionary to reformist mentality"
A necessary and welcome tactical adjustment

q: Nehru argued that a genuine anti-imperialist struggle required incorporating which additional dimension?
o: The class struggle of peasants and workers, organised through kisan sabhas and trade unions affiliated with the Congress
Exclusive reliance on urban middle-class leadership
Abandonment of all mass organisations in favour of elite negotiation
Cooperation with British capitalists to strengthen the economy first

q: The 'Struggle-Truce-Struggle' (S-T-S) strategy, associated with Gandhi and much of the Congress leadership, envisioned:
o: Struggle only in provinces where Congress held a majority
A mass struggle phase followed by a truce phase to allow recuperation, before resuming struggle if the government failed to respond
Permanent truce with no further mass action
Continuous, uninterrupted mass struggle with no truce phase ever

q: In contrast to the S-T-S strategy, Nehru proposed which alternative approach?
o: Alliance with the Muslim League against the Congress
Immediate acceptance of dominion status
A Struggle-Victory (S-V) strategy involving continuous direct action without any interposing constitutionalist phase
A complete boycott of the Congress organisation

q: Gandhi ultimately reconciled Congress differences over council entry by:
o: Banning all forms of council participation permanently
Permitting Congressmen who could not offer satyagraha or do constructive work to express their patriotic energies through council work
Expelling all Swarajist-minded members from the Congress
Insisting all Congressmen must contest elections regardless of preference

q: The Government of India Act, 1935, passed by the British Parliament in August 1935, proposed an All India Federation comprising:
o: A federation limited to Bengal, Bombay, and Madras presidencies
Only the princely states, excluding British India
Only British Indian provinces, excluding princely states entirely
All British Indian provinces, chief commissioner's provinces, and the princely states

q: Why did the All India Federation proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935 never actually come into being?
o: The British Parliament repealed the federal provisions before implementation
The Indian National Congress vetoed the federation formally
World War II made federation legally impossible from the outset
The conditions requiring sufficient princely states (accounting for 50% of their total population) to join were never fulfilled

q: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, at the federal level, which subjects were classified as 'reserved', to be administered exclusively by the governor-general?
o: Education, health and agriculture
Foreign affairs, defence, tribal areas and ecclesiastical affairs
Local government and industry
Currency and taxation

q: Under the 1935 Act's federal legislature, the bicameral structure consisted of the Council of States (upper house) and the Federal Assembly (lower house). Which of the following is correctly noted about their composition and election method?
o: Election to the Council of States was direct while election to the Federal Assembly was indirect — an unusual reversal of typical practice
The Federal Assembly was directly elected while the Council of States was entirely nominated by princes
Both houses were directly elected by universal adult suffrage
Both houses were entirely nominated by the governor-general

q: Under provincial autonomy in the 1935 Act, ministers administering provincial subjects were made:
o: Answerable only to the governor, with no legislative accountability
Directly appointed by the British Parliament
Answerable to and removable by an adverse vote of the provincial legislature
Permanently appointed with no removal mechanism

q: Which of the following is a key criticism of the Government of India Act, 1935, as noted in the chapter's evaluation?
o: Its extension of communal electorates promoted separatist tendencies that ultimately contributed to the partition of India
It enfranchised the majority of the Indian population
It abolished all forms of communal representation, angering minority communities
It granted full parliamentary sovereignty to Indian legislatures

q: Jawaharlal Nehru's famous critique of the Government of India Act, 1935 described it metaphorically as:
o: "An empty vessel"
"A car, all brakes and no engine"
"A house of cards"
"A ship without a rudder"

q: Which of the following describes the long-term British strategic thinking behind the reforms embodied in the 1935 Act?
o: To grant immediate dominion status and withdraw from India entirely
To integrate segments of the national movement into constitutional structures, thereby weakening the impetus for extra-legal mass struggle
To unite all Indian political groups into a single unified party
To completely dismantle the Indian National Congress as an organisation

q: In the second stage debate (early 1937), the central question dividing Congress leftists and moderates was:
o: Whether to merge with the Muslim League
Whether to dissolve the Congress altogether
Whether the Congress should accept ministerial office in provinces if it won a majority in provincial elections
Whether to boycott the 1937 elections entirely

q: Nehru, Subhash Bose, and Congress socialists/communists opposed office acceptance chiefly on the ground that:
o: It would mean assuming responsibility without real power, undermining the movement's revolutionary character
It contradicted the Congress's earlier support for the Nehru Report
It would immediately trigger British suppression of the Congress
It was legally prohibited under the 1935 Act

q: As a counter-strategy, the leftists who opposed straightforward office acceptance proposed:
o: Immediate armed insurrection against provincial governments
Complete withdrawal from all electoral activity
Entering the councils with the aim of creating deadlocks to make the Act unworkable — an older Swarajist-style strategy
Formation of a rival constituent assembly

q: Proponents of office acceptance argued that provincial ministries, despite their limited powers, could serve which useful purpose?
o: Abolish the need for any future mass movement
Achieve full independence for India immediately
Replace the Indian National Congress as the primary nationalist body
Promote constructive work and prevent the administrative field from being left entirely to pro-government reactionary forces

q: The Congress sessions at Lucknow (early 1936) and Faizpur (late 1937) resolved to fight the 1937 elections while adopting which stance towards the 1935 Act?
o: Formal acceptance of dominion status under the Act
Complete boycott of the elections
Full cooperation with the Act's provisions
Not to submit to or cooperate with the constitution, but to combat it both inside and outside the legislatures until it was ended

q: The February 1937 provincial elections were held in how many provinces, and approximately how many people were enfranchised?
o: Eleven provinces, with about 30.1 million people (14% of the population) enfranchised
Five provinces, with about 5 million people enfranchised
Eleven provinces, with only male voters enfranchised
All of British India as a single constituency, with universal suffrage

q: The Congress manifesto for the 1937 elections included commitments to:
o: Continuation of the salt tax and existing agrarian structure
Release of political prisoners, removal of gender/caste-based disabilities, agrarian reform, and rights to form trade unions and strike
Full cooperation with the governor's reserved powers
Support for separate electorates for all communities
